text:
Alex: Ran an overnight benchmark for the 30B q4f16 bring-up across two Dedicated pools: us-west2 (H100) and eu-central1 (H100a). Goal was to measure steady-state qps per GPU, p50/p95/p99 latency, and kernel choices so we can size pools for a 120 qps regional SLA with a safe autoscale runway.
Lia: Nice — can you paste the raw latency buckets and the kernel/runtime flags you used?
Alex: Sure. Test config: 2048 context, streaming=false, kv-cache warm, max_batch_tokens=2048, continuous_batching enabled. Kernel selection: fused-attn-v2 on H100, fallback to matmul-path on older boxes.
Alex: Raw summary (one-line CSV rows):
```
region,gpu_type,qps_target,qps_per_gpu,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,kernel,threads_per_gpu
us-west2,H100,120,9.8,18,62,124,fused-attn-v2,4
eu-central1,H100a,120,7.9,22,82,190,matmul-path,3
```
Alex: From these runs we estimate: us-west2 needs ceil(120/9.8)=13 GPUs -> recommend 16 GPUs (25% spare headroom + 1 spare for AZ failover). eu-central1 needs ceil(120/7.9)=16 -> recommend 20 GPUs.
Mike: Did you consider concurrency limits? p99 blows up above 50 concurrent requests on eu-central1 in the matmul path. What concurrency were you measuring?
Alex: We capped per-GPU concurrency to 50 in the eu run (3 threads_per_gpu). Above that p99 tails get long because matmul-path has worse kernel fusion and KV eviction jitter. us-west kept 4 threads_per_gpu and stayed stable up to 70 concurrency.
Claudia: How much of the difference is kernel vs region network egress? Any cross-checked runs with identical kernel forced?
Alex: Good call. I forced fused-attn-v2 on eu-central1 on a small sample (shadow run) and saw p95 improve ~18% but p99 still ~30% worse than us-west2. So ~half the gap is kernel, half looks infra/noise + instance family differences.
Henry: Cost note — rough monthly delta if we follow recommendations: us-west2 (16 H100) = ~$32k, eu-central1 (20 H100a) = ~$44k. Upsizing eu region buys latency reliability but increases committed spend by ~38%.
Lia: Autoscale runway — what buffer do you recommend for bursts? 25% seems common but maybe we need more for nightly spikes.
Alex: For Dedicated I'd do: baseline = recommended_gpus, runway = +25% for surge, emergency buffer = +2 GPUs for AZ failover. So formula: deployed = ceil(baseline * 1.25) + 2. For eu that gives 20 -> deployed 27. That's aggressive but keeps p99 under target during 3x sustained spike windows observed in production traces.
Mike: Can we instead tune batching/latency SLO and accept slightly higher p99 to avoid that many GPUs? Like cap batch size smaller during spikes?
Alex: Yes — alternate plan: smart autoscale + dynamic batch cap. If we reduce max_batch_tokens by 25% at high concurrency we recover ~12% qps per GPU for eu run and delay scale-up by ~1-2 GPUs. Still recommend runway but can shave 2-3 GPUs off deployed count.
bench-bot: Upload complete: /benchmarks/30B_q4f16/overnight/2723456789/results.json (summary attached).
Claudia: Please add the perf-degradation test for matmul-path + KV-cache stress to the onboarding checklist. We missed a regression last time because we didn't simulate multi-tenancy tails.
Alex: Will add. Action items: 1) Update Dedicated sizing calc in runbook with the deployed formula and include region-specific qps_per_gpu constants; 2) Schedule kernel sweep (fused-attn-v2 vs matmul-path) on eu next week; 3) Add dynamic batch cap experiment to autoscale playbook; 4) Open infra ticket to validate H100a kernel builds.

Henry: I'll model cost vs 95th-latency SLA and share a chart in the next sync. If we can accept p95=100ms in eu we can drop ~4 GPUs.
Lia: Great thread. Can you also drop the small CSV and the commands you used for the run in the ticket? Makes it easier for SRE to reproduce.
Alex: Done — added commands and env file to the ticket. Will follow up Monday with the kernel-sweep schedule. :calendar:
